summary:
MARSATLAS is an interactive Martian exploration and survival system designed to help users explore the surface of Mars, with a focus on the Jezero Crater region. Inspired by the challenges of future human exploration, the project brings together a Mars surface map, mission information, waypoint exploration, approximate route planning, and a science catalog in one mission-control interface.

Users can explore Martian regions, examine mission waypoints, plan potential routes, and review scientific information relevant to exploration. The platform also includes simulated mission telemetry and browser-based demo reports to illustrate how mission information could be organized and monitored.

MARSATLAS aims to make Martian geography and exploration data more accessible through an intuitive interactive experience. It demonstrates how mapping technology and software can support mission planning, scientific discovery, and preparation for future human exploration of Mars.
details:
MARSATLAS is built as a mission-control prototype that brings Martian exploration information into one interactive interface. The application focuses on Jezero Crater, while also providing a catalog of other notable Martian regions.

The platform includes an interactive Mars surface map with satellite imagery layers, a mission dashboard, an approximate route planner, a science explorer, and mission reports. Users can explore geographic regions, review curated waypoints, examine scientific reference information, and view simulated mission telemetry. The map includes imagery layers from NASA Solar System Treks, including Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX and HiRISE mosaics, Viking MDIM 2.1, and Mars Global Surveyor MOLA shaded relief.

The project was developed using React 18, JavaScript, Vite, OpenLayers, Node.js, Express, and MongoDB/Mongoose. It uses a modular frontend and backend architecture, with fallback data for demonstration purposes.

MARSATLAS aims to make Mars geography and exploration information easier to understand and explore. Its creative approach combines planetary mapping, scientific references, and a mission-control interface to demonstrate how digital tools can support future exploration planning. Telemetry and example mission reports are simulated; the prototype does not provide live NASA telemetry.
